dimensions.evidenceA: Covet is repeated for house and wife.
dimensions.evidenceB: Covet introduces wife; desire introduces house and field.
dimensions.label: Verb sequence

evidence.observation: Exodus first forbids coveting the neighbor’s house, then repeats covet before wife, servants, animals, and anything belonging to the neighbor.
Deuteronomy first forbids coveting the neighbor’s wife, then says not to desire house, field, servants, animals, or anything belonging to the neighbor.

record.tension: Exodus places house before wife under repeated coveting language, while Deuteronomy places wife before house and introduces a second verb and the field.
record.title: What is named first in the command against coveting?
